records.content: Kantesti — AI-Powered Blood Test Analyzer Experience AI-powered blood test analysis and interpretation with multilingual health insight reports. Kantesti helps users better understand blood test results with clear explanations, abnormal value highlights, trend insights and easy-to-read reports in 75+ languages. The platform uses modern cloud, AI infrastructure, and security services, with technology references including Microsoft, NVIDIA Inception, Google Cloud, and Cloudflare. 100,000+ Downloads on Google Play Use Kantesti for AI-powered blood test explanations and easy-to-read informational health reports. Now available on Android with support for 75+ languages. Kantesti® AI Blood Test Analyzer Informational Blood Test Explanation AI Blood Test Analyzer: your lab results explained in plain language Kantesti® is an AI blood test analyzer that turns lab results into clear, multilingual health insight reports, so you can understand your blood test results. Upload a PDF, JPG or PNG and receive AI blood test interpretation with abnormal value highlights and plain-language explanations in 100+ languages, usually within a few minutes. New: Kantesti Voice reads the key points aloud, in your report's language. - First analysis free - No credit card required - Educational information, not a diagnosis - New - 100+report languages - PDF · JPG · PNGlab report uploads - ~2 minaudio summary, ~40 s free - Freefirst analysis, no credit card Why choose the Kantesti AI blood test analyzer Clear AI Blood Test Analysis Plain-language explanation of your blood test results with abnormal value highlights, structured summaries, trend tracking and wellness context. Biomarker Explanations Easy-to-read summaries that compare reported values with the reference ranges shown in your uploaded lab report. Listen to Your Report New Kantesti Voice reads the key points of your interpretation aloud in your report's language: your results in brief, then what to do next. Multilingual Report Support Supports PDF, JPG and PNG blood test uploads and generates clear health insight reports in 100+ languages. Privacy-Focused Security Built with encrypted upload flows and privacy-conscious data handling. Your health data is never sold. Built for Health Conversations Designed to make lab results easier to understand and discuss with a licensed healthcare professional. How Kantesti® AI blood test interpretation works Three simple steps to turn your lab results into structured educational health insights. - 1 Upload your lab resultsDrop your blood test in PDF, JPG or PNG. We securely process all major lab formats. - 2 AI analysis & interpretationThe AI reads reported biomarkers and compares values with the reference ranges shown in your uploaded document where available. - 3 Read it, or listen to itReceive a structured educational report with abnormal value highlights, trend context and discussion points, then press play to hear the key points. New Kantesti Voice Listen to your blood test results, read aloud in your language Kantesti Voice is an AI-generated voice that reads the AI interpretation of your blood test report aloud, in the language your report was written in. It reads only your report's own educational interpretation, adds no new medical content, and the player always labels it as an AI-generated voice, not a doctor. - 1 Your results in brief Free previewAbout 40 seconds. A short summary of what your results say and the findings that stand out. Comes with your free demo report. - 2 New AI-generated voice · not a doctor Listen to your AI interpretation Your report explained aloud, in the language you chose Caption preview without sound. The real voice plays inside your own report.Real Kantesti Voice audio: part 1 of a fictional sample patient's report, read from its own AI interpretation. Educational information, not a diagnosis. Transcript (English audio) · part 1 · fictional sample patient The patient presents with a clinically significant normocytic anemia (HGB 10.90 g/dL, HCT 32.60%) in the presence of an elevated erythrocyte sedimentation rate (ESR 53.00 mm/h), suggesting an underlying chronic inflammatory or autoimmune process. The ESR of 53.00 mm/h is significantly elevated for a 67-year-old female (age-adjusted upper limit is approximately 30 mm/h). These findings are highly suggestive of a chronic inflammatory process that requires urgent diagnostic investigation. - English - Türkçe - Deutsch - Español - Français - Italiano - Português - العربية - हिन्दी - 日本語 - Nederlands - Polski - and many more - In your report's languageThe voice speaks the language your report is written in. - Private by designYour own report's audio plays only inside your web report, with no audio file to download, and is deleted on a fixed schedule. - Never slows your reportAudio is prepared in the background. If it cannot be made, your report arrives exactly as before. - Clearly labelled as AIThe player always shows "AI-generated voice · not a doctor". Get your free AI blood test analysis today Turn complex lab results into clear explanations, reference-range context and easy-to-read report summaries with Kantesti®, then listen to the key points in your own language. Get free analysis now First analysis free · No credit card required Upload your blood test results for a free AI analysis AI-powered blood test interpretation · 100+ languages · Results in a few minutes · Audio summary included Secure upload flow · privacy-conscious processing - Fast analysisClear report generation - AI health insightsRange-aware explanations - Plain-English resultsNo confusing jargon - Audio summaryFree preview in your demo report Also in your report: Biological Blood Age and the Body Map Two additions generated by the Kantesti® AI engine from the values already present in your uploaded document. Both are educational context to help you prepare a conversation with a licensed healthcare professional. Neither is a diagnosis, a screening result, a disease-risk score or a prediction of any health outcome. The free report previews both; premium reports show them in full. Kantesti® Biological Blood Age A blood age calculated from your own panel blood age Often searched as a blood age or biological age calculator, this figure is calculated from the biomarker values in your report together with the age on your report (or the one you enter): with the published PhenoAge formula when your panel includes the nine markers it needs, otherwise as an estimate whose method the report names. The report also names the markers that shaped the number, so you can see exactly where it came from. - Estimated from the values in your own uploaded blood test - Shows which reported markers influenced the estimate - The fewer markers a panel carries, the more indicative the figure Educational estimate only. It is not a clinical measurement of ageing and does not diagnose, screen for, monitor or predict any disease, health outcome or life expectancy. Discuss any marker it highlights with a qualified healthcare professional. Kantesti® Body Map Where each out-of-range value points on the body - Heart & blood vesselsLDL-Cholesterol above the range shown in the document - Pancreas & blood sugarHbA1c above the range shown in the document - Kidneys & electrolytesPotassium and magnesium below the range shown When a reported value sits outside the reference range printed in your document, the body map draws it on a human silhouette and names the organ or body system that laboratory marker is commonly associated with, with a legend you can read at a glance. Illustration for orientation and education only. The highlighted areas indicate which body system a marker is commonly associated with. They do not locate, diagnose, screen for or rule out any condition in any organ. Hidden indices: clinical ratios a lab print-out does not print Alongside the two new sections, Kantesti® computes well-known clinical ratios and indices (up to 18, depending on your panel) arithmetically from values already present in your report, and shows each one together with the markers it was derived from. - Non-HDL cholesterolFrom total and HDL cholesterol - Total/HDL ratioCastelli index, from the lipid panel - TG/HDL ratioFrom triglycerides and HDL cholesterol - Atherogenic index of plasmalog(TG/HDL) from the same two markers - Remnant cholesterolFrom total, HDL and LDL cholesterol - Estimated average glucoseDerived arithmetically from HbA1c - eGFR (CKD-EPI 2021)From creatinine, age and sex - Shown with their sourceEvery index names the values it was built from These indices come from published formulas applied to your own reported values. They are educational indicators for discussion with a qualified healthcare professional, not screening results, diagnoses or treatment guidance. See what an example report looks like An illustrative, anonymized example showing the structure of a Kantesti educational health insight report. It is sample content only and not a diagnosis, disease-risk score or treatment recommendation. Example Biomarker Summary Educational overview based on sample lab values only Summary Example discussion areas Example Biological Blood Age AI-estimated from the sample panel and the stated age · educational only blood age This example figure is an educational estimate produced from the sample values only. It is not a clinical measurement of ageing and does not diagnose, screen for, monitor or predict any disease, health outcome or life expectancy. Example Body Map Which body system each out-of-range sample value relates to - Heart & blood vesselsLDL-Cholesterol above the displayed example range - Pancreas & blood sugarGlucose-related markers shown for context - Vitamins & nutritionVitamin D below the displayed example range Illustration for orientation only. The highlighted areas show which organ or body system the flagged sample markers are commonly associated with. They are not a diagnosis and do not locate or rule out any condition. Values to Review 4 Biomarker Discussion Overview Illustrative overview based on example biomarker patterns, not disease prediction Introduction Blood test summary In this illustrative sample, Total Cholesterol (218 mg/dL), LDL-C (142 mg/dL) and Triglyceride (156 mg/dL) are above the displayed reference thresholds. Fasting glucose (98 mg/dL) and HbA1c (5.3%) are shown within the displayed ranges. This is educational context only and does not diagnose, rule out or predict any disease. Hemoglobin (14.8 g/dL) and MCV (87.8 fl) appear within the example reference ranges. AST, ALT, GGT, creatinine and GFR are also shown within the displayed intervals. These values should be reviewed in the full clinical context by a qualified healthcare professional. Vitamin D (25-OH) is shown at 24.5 ng/ml, below the example reference range of 30.0–70.0 ng/ml. This may be useful as a discussion point with a qualified healthcare professional; supplement decisions should not be made from this example report alone. Educational Biomarker Context Plain-language context for sample results The lipid section highlights LDL-C and Total Cholesterol because they are above the displayed example thresholds. The report explains how related lipid markers are commonly reviewed together and suggests discussing persistent out-of-range values with a clinician. The glucose-related values in this sample appear within the displayed reference information. This does not rule out metabolic disease; it simply shows how the report can summarize values for professional review. CRP and TSH are shown with their example reference context. The report does not determine the cause of lipid changes or exclude thyroid-related conditions; those questions require qualified clinical assessment. Key Discussion Points Vitamin D (25-OH) is below the displayed example range and may be a useful topic for clinician discussion, especially when reviewed with symptoms, history, medicines and other laboratory values. Triglyceride is slightly above the displayed example threshold. The report can help a user prepare questions about diet, lifestyle, follow-up testing and professional review. GFR and creatinine appear within the displayed example ranges. This does not confirm kidney health or exclude disease; it only shows how reference-range context can be presented clearly. Full Lab Values Every measured biomarker against its reference range Biomarker Detail Where each value sits on its range, with what it means Reference: <130 mg/dl LDL carries cholesterol to tissues; values above the displayed range are commonly discussed as part of cardiovascular wellness review. Reference: 30–70 ng/ml 25-hydroxyvitamin D is commonly used to review vitamin D status and may be discussed with a qualified healthcare professional. Reference: 40–100 mg/dl HDL transports excess cholesterol back to the liver for removal; higher levels are generally favorable. Reference: 70–99 mg/dl Fasting glucose is commonly reviewed with HbA1c and other context when discussing blood sugar patterns. Reference: 13.5–17.5 g/dl Hemoglobin carries oxygen from the lungs to the body; this example value sits within the displayed reference range. Reference: 0.27–4.2 mU/l TSH is commonly reviewed with thyroid hormone values and symptoms when discussing thyroid function. Discussion Points & General Wellness Context Educational prompts for clinician discussion 🩺 Discuss with a clinician - Ask a licensed healthcare professional whether Vitamin D supplementation is appropriate for your situation. - Consider discussing lipid profile follow-up timing with your primary care provider. - Use this report as informational support, not as a diagnosis or treatment decision. 🥗 Lifestyle & Diet - Discuss heart-healthy dietary patterns, fiber intake and omega-3 sources with a qualified healthcare professional if lipid markers are repeatedly out of range. - Consider asking a healthcare professional what level of physical activity is appropriate for your situation. - Ask whether vitamin D intake, safe sun exposure or supplementation is appropriate before making changes. The Kantesti® AI blood test analyzer, explained An AI blood test analyzer is a tool that uses artificial intelligence to read laboratory blood test results and explain them in plain language. Kantesti® delivers AI blood test interpretation for uploaded PDF, JPG or PNG reports: the AI reviews reported values, compares them with available reference ranges where shown, and creates a structured educational report with health insights, trend context and discussion points, which you can read or listen to. - Kantesti Voice New - Reads the key points of your interpretation aloud in the language of your report, in web reports. Part 1, your results in brief (about 40 seconds), comes free with your demo report; part 2, next steps to discuss with your doctor (about 80 seconds), is included in premium reports. It is an AI-generated voice, not a doctor, and it reads only your report's own educational interpretation. - What it is - An AI blood test analyzer that reads lab results and explains reported biomarkers in plain language. - How interpretation works - You upload a report, the AI reviews each reported biomarker and explains it against available reference ranges where shown. - Regulatory status - Currently under regulatory and validation review. Not currently CE-marked or UKCA-marked. The service provides informational support only; it is not a diagnostic test and does not diagnose or treat disease. - Biomarkers covered - Explains a wide range of reported biomarkers across lipids, metabolic, hematology, liver, kidney, thyroid and vitamins. - Speed - A full AI blood test interpretation usually within a few minutes, available 24/7. The audio summary is prepared in the background and never delays the report. - Supported uploads - Supports common PDF, JPG and PNG lab result documents from different report layouts worldwide. - Languages - Health insight reports in 100+ languages. The audio summary is read in the language of your report. - Privacy & security - Encrypted upload flow and privacy-conscious handling; your health data is never sold. Audio plays inside your report only and is not offered as a download. - Cost - Your first analysis is free, with no credit card: it shows your flagged values and a preview of the rest; premium reports unlock the full interpretation. - Biological Blood Age - A blood age calculated from the values in your report and the age on your report or the one you enter (the published PhenoAge formula when the nine markers it needs are present, otherwise an estimate whose method the report names), shown as educational context. It is not a clinical measurement of ageing or a prediction of any health outcome. - Body Map - Out-of-range values are drawn on a human silhouette with a legend naming the organ or body system each marker relates to. Illustration for orientation only, never a diagnosis. - Hidden indices - Clinical ratios such as non-HDL cholesterol, TG/HDL, atherogenic index of plasma, estimated average glucose and eGFR, computed from values already present in your report. Common ways people use Kantesti Practical ways Kantesti® can organize blood test terminology, reference-range context and follow-up questions before a professional review. Illustrative use cases, not customer reviews. Preparing for an appointment Kantesti can make blood test information easier to review and discuss by turning biomarker values into structured, plain-language appointment questions. Organizing glucose and HbA1c over time Users can organize A1C and glucose values over time and prepare clearer follow-up questions for a licensed healthcare professional. Reviewing nutrition markers Plain-language explanations can help users understand vitamin, iron and nutrition-related markers before discussing next steps with a qualified professional.
